lines: Q: What's the hardest part of meals for you? Or something else.
A: The hardest part is deciding what to cook daily and remembering to order the groceries.

Q: Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the plan and the shopping list fit you from the first week, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
A: Zepto mostly, Instamart when something's not on Zepto.
A: Sign in later maybe.
Q: Which is your main app, and which do you use when something isn't there?
A: Zepto is the main one, Instamart when Zepto doesn't have it.
Q: I have Shiva (38), Ankita (35), Agastya (6) and Gowri Shankar (63) eating at home. Anyone else who eats at home, or anyone who doesn't?
A: That's everyone who eats at home regularly, no one else.
Q: Lakshmi cooks Mon-Sat: Breakfast and Lunch at 7am, Dinner at 6pm. Is that right, and does the cook come for any other meals?
A: That's right, breakfast and lunch in the morning, dinner in the evening. No other meals.
Q: Is the cook short of time, say off to the next house, so only a dish or two in the morning?
A: Yes, she has about an hour in the morning. Breakfast plus at most two dishes for lunch.
A: actually Lakshmi comes at 7:30
Q: On Sunday, when the cook doesn't come, who cooks? Or is a meal eaten out?
A: Ankita makes a quick breakfast and dinner on Sunday. Lunch we eat out.
Q: What did the children have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Agastya had idli with chutney twice, dosa, poha, upma, and aloo paratha on Saturday. Milk every morning.
Q: The children's lunch over the past week, or their school tiffin?
A: Agastya's school tiffin last week: paratha rolls, besan cheela, mini idlis, vegetable sandwich, lemon rice on Friday.
Q: The children's dinner over the past week?
A: Agastya's dinner is usually what we adults eat: chapati with dal or a sabzi, less spicy. When he's tired, curd rice.
Q: What did the adults have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Adults had a mixed breakfast - idli, dosa, poha, upma, sandwich. Father had ragi dosa and oats. Weekend parathas.
Q: The adults' lunch over the past week?
A: Lunch was south indian - rice, sambar, sabji. Bisi bele bath on Saturday. Father has the same with less rice.
Q: The adults' dinner over the past week?
A: Dinner was roti with gravy or dry sabji. Palak dal, bhindi, aloo gobi, chole once.
A: Father has two phulkas, no rice at night.
Q: Is anyone on a diet? High protein, low carb, diabetic, anything a doctor asked for.
A: Father is diabetic, so less rice, no sugar, millets are good for him. Also less salt.
Q: Besides that diet, do the elders eat anything differently: less salt, softer food, no onion or garlic, a fasting day?
A: Father has less salt too. Onion and garlic are fine.
A: He fasts every Thursday till evening, then a light dinner.
Q: Any food rules for the house? Veg, egg or non-veg days, fasting days, allergies, a dish someone won't touch.
A: Vegetarian, no eggs at home. No mushrooms.
A: Agastya's school is nut-free, so his tiffin can't have nuts. Father fasts Thursdays till evening.
Q: How often do you order in, and on which days?
A: Once a week, usually Saturday dinner from Swiggy.
Q: Does anything come on a subscription, like Country Delight or a milkman?
A: Yes, Country Delight milk, 1 litre every morning.
